correctness.rationale: With A=E[(Y-X)1_{X<Y}] and B=E[(X-Y)1_{X>Y}], A-B=E[(Y-X)(1_{X<Y}+1_{X>Y})]=E[Y-X] because the equality event contributes zero. Integrability makes both finite and covers zero-probability comparison events via unconditional truncations. Thus A>=B iff E[X]<=E[Y], without independence or regularity. Equality of both directions is equality of means.
